name: cruisemapper-ships-scraper
what_it_holds: Node.js/Python scraper targeting cruisemapper.com for cruise ship data extraction (ship specs, presumably schedules/positions since cruisemapper tracks live ship positions and itineraries). MIT licence, updated Apr 2026, 1 star. No committed dataset seen, tool only.
why_useful: cruisemapper.com aggregates live ship tracking/itinerary data across all major lines (NCLH/CCL/RCL); a working scraper against it could in principle build a port-call/schedule panel, but this repo ships no data and scraping a commercial site is a ToS question per repo rules.
themes: Cruise line data: NCLH / Carnival / Royal Caribbean advance ticket sales, capacity, occupancy, cruise schedules and port calls
why_all: cruisemapper.com aggregates live ship tracking/itinerary data across all major lines (NCLH/CCL/RCL); a working scraper against it could in principle build a port-call/schedule panel, but this repo ships no data and scraping a commercial site is a ToS question per repo rules.

name: cruise-ship-data-extractor
what_it_holds: Node.js scraper (via ScraperAPI, a paid proxy service) extracting data on ~1,155 cruise ships: images, amenities, and specs. No occupancy, pricing, or schedule fields evident; no data committed to the repo itself. Updated Apr 2026, 1 star.
why_useful: Ship-count/fleet-roster data at best; no booking, ADR, or occupancy signal. Marginal even as a fleet-capacity proxy (could sum berths across NCLH/CCL/RCL ships if specs include passenger capacity) but requires running the scraper (paid API) and no sample output is visible.
size_hint: Code only; target ~1,155 ship records if run
themes: Cruise line data: NCLH / Carnival / Royal Caribbean advance ticket sales, capacity, occupancy, cruise schedules and port calls
why_all: Ship-count/fleet-roster data at best; no booking, ADR, or occupancy signal. Marginal even as a fleet-capacity proxy (could sum berths across NCLH/CCL/RCL ships if specs include passenger capacity) but requires running the scraper (paid API) and no sample output is visible.

name: ItineraryWatch
what_it_holds: Monitors cruise itineraries matching customer-provided search criteria (a price/availability watcher, not a stored panel). MIT licence, updated Jul 2026, 0 stars.
why_useful: Conceptually close to a booking-curve/price-tracking tool (relevant to 'reserve now pay later' / advance-sale analogues) but it is a personal alert tool with no committed historical data and unclear source coverage.
themes: Cruise line data: NCLH / Carnival / Royal Caribbean advance ticket sales, capacity, occupancy, cruise schedules and port calls
why_all: Conceptually close to a booking-curve/price-tracking tool (relevant to 'reserve now pay later' / advance-sale analogues) but it is a personal alert tool with no committed historical data and unclear source coverage.

name: vessel-traffic-mcp
what_it_holds: Read-only MCP server normalizing vessel identity, AIS-style positions, port calls, and shipping schedules across a provider tier system: fixture data (deterministic test data, no network), public opt-in browser-captured adapters (MyShipTracking, Tradlinx, AIsFriends), and BYOK commercial APIs (MarineTraffic, VesselFinder, AISStream, AISHub, BarentsWatch, SeaRates, Routescanner, VesselAPI). No bulk data committed beyond test fixtures. MIT licensed, 101 commits.
why_useful: A generic client/normalizer for AIS-based port-call and vessel-schedule data; could in principle be pointed at a specific cruise ship's IMO/MMSI to derive port-dwell-time / itinerary-pace as an occupancy-timing proxy, but requires paid API keys (BYOK) for anything beyond fixtures, and explicitly avoids bypassing paywalls.
themes: Cruise line data: NCLH / Carnival / Royal Caribbean advance ticket sales, capacity, occupancy, cruise schedules and port calls
why_all: A generic client/normalizer for AIS-based port-call and vessel-schedule data; could in principle be pointed at a specific cruise ship's IMO/MMSI to derive port-dwell-time / itinerary-pace as an occupancy-timing proxy, but requires paid API keys (BYOK) for anything beyond fixtures, and explicitly avoids bypassing paywalls.

name: timonelo
what_it_holds: A 'cruise intelligence' knowledge-graph platform (Python/Pydantic backend, TypeScript/React frontend) organizing evidence about ships, cabins, routes and ports under knowledge/ships/, knowledge/evidence/ (SHA-256-verified artifacts), and data/hypotheses/ (explicitly quarantined, non-canonical). No dataset size/time-span documented; 230 commits on develop branch. MIT licensed.
why_useful: Early-stage structured schema for cruise ship/route/port facts with a verification discipline; not a ready dataset but worth watching if it accumulates a real corpus of route/capacity facts.
themes: Cruise line data: NCLH / Carnival / Royal Caribbean advance ticket sales, capacity, occupancy, cruise schedules and port calls
why_all: Early-stage structured schema for cruise ship/route/port facts with a verification discipline; not a ready dataset but worth watching if it accumulates a real corpus of route/capacity facts.
